clue.text: Court risks show of passion?

parts.note: to show a film or a part is to play it
something done with fire is done with passion

explanation.surface: A question about whether a display of ardour is a dangerous thing in a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a noun (a law court or tennis court) but is a verb here: to court risks is to invite them.
explanation.definitionFit: To play with fire is an idiom for knowingly inviting danger, which is what courting risks means.

clue.text: Merger of corporation and board is appropriate for consumers

indicators.note: the two words are merged so that the letter they could share appears only once where they meet

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a big belly, a pot
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Business-speak about a corporate merger with a board being good for customers.
explanation.walkthrough: POT ends in T and TABLE starts with T; the merger overlaps them on that shared T.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable means fit to drink, so it is suitable for those who consume it.

clue.text: Food intake's initially lowered through illness

indicators.note: in a down entry, a letter moved further along the word sits lower in the grid

parts.note: an ailment is an illness

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word intake's

parts.note: first letter of intake's

explanation.surface: A diet note: someone eating less because they are ill.
explanation.walkthrough: In AILMENT the I is second; 'lowered' moves it one place down the column, through the L, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment, which is what food provides.

clue.text: Lying Liberal stops supporting women's sport

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting part sits below, so the women's letter goes on top

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: the Liberal letter stops up the other word, plugging a gap inside it

parts.note: lying down is resting

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a dishonest Liberal stops backing women's sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is a combat sport in which two people grapple.

clue.text: Upset about university student's bloomer

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the upset word goes round the others

parts.note: to upset a cart is to tip it
L, for learner, is the usual crossword student

explanation.surface: A university student upset by a blunder, a 'bloomer'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, the British slang sense; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower that blooms is a bloomer, and the tulip is a classic spring flower.

clue.text: Female drinker is a flighty creature

parts.note: a lapper is one who laps up liquid, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A woman who drinks is called giddy and irresponsible.
explanation.walkthrough: A flapper was a fashionable, carefree young woman of the 1920s; the word also means a young bird learning to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Flapper describes both a fledgling bird trying its wings and a frivolous jazz-age girl, both flighty.

clue.text: What production company makes available, free or on rental

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a film or record a company puts out

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A film company making its product available to buy outright or to rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and a charade: the word is a new film or record, means to set free, and is built from RE and LEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio's new film is a release, and to release a prisoner is to set them free.

clue.text: Ring in very good condition?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ring the way a bell does, read literally
second meaning: the idiom for being perfectly healthy or sound

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a ring is exactly the sound a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in perfect health or working order, and a bell's note is literally a ring.

clue.text: Summary statement of public policy

parts.note: when news is out it is public
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A short statement setting out what a government plans to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a brief sketch of the main points, which is a summary.

clue.text: Publication that's produced by the Greens?

definitions.text: Publication that's produced by the Greens?

parts.words: Publication that's produced by the Greens?
parts.note: a political party hands out pamphlets, and green plants put out small new leaves

explanation.walkthrough: The Green Party seems to be handing out a pamphlet; read literally, greenery grows small leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out, and botanically a small young leaf.

clue.text: Most of those people look, after drunk nurses start to dance

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
most of means drop the last letter

parts.note: they means those people

explanation.surface: People looking after a drunk who is having a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' seems to mean nurse, but its own letters are the ones rearranged; 'nurses' is the container signal, and 'Most of' trims the pronoun for those people.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the floor is to get up and begin dancing, as on a dance floor.

clue.text: Most illustrious reporter's experience bringing happiness to audience

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so it is what we hear that counts

parts.note: to know something is to have experienced it

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: blessed means favoured, bringing happiness

explanation.surface: A reporter's story about an experience that delighted those watching.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOW sounds like NO, and BLESSED is said just like the old spelling BLEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblest is the superlative of noble, so it means most distinguished or eminent.

clue.text: What inspires rumour about football manager?

parts.note: Pep Guardiola is a famous football manager
talk is gossip or rumour

explanation.surface: Asking which piece of gossip about a football boss gets people fired up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pep Guardiola manages Manchester City; 'about' just joins rumour to the man it concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: A pep talk is a short speech meant to encourage and motivate a team.

clue.text: Signal change when head of state takes more central role

indicators.note: the head of state moves inward, nearer the middle of the word

parts.note: to alter is to change
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: A political shift signalled when a monarch becomes more involved.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual head of state; moving the royal pair inward is what 'takes more central role' means.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, such as a siren or alarm.

clue.text: Revolutionary books introduced by popular and powerful mass movement?

indicators.note: the books come after the other pieces, which lead them in

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a surge is a powerful rush of a mass, as of water or a crowd
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Revolutionary books spread by a strong popular movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel fighting against the government, a revolutionary.

clue.text: Exploded silly myths without a trace of merit in an elegant way

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and come down in a new order
without means the letter is taken away
a trace of means just the first letter

parts.note: first letter of merit

explanation.surface: Debunking foolish legends with flair, and with no merit at all.
explanation.walkthrough: SILLYMYTHS less the M from 'a trace of merit' leaves letters that 'Exploded' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylishly means with style and polish, which is elegantly.

clue.text: In the morning, lay around conserving energy to my surprise

parts.note: AM means in the morning

indicators.note: conserving means keeping something inside
around means the letters of lay are moved about

parts.note: zing is energy or zest

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to find themselves lazing around in the morning, saving energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazingly is an adverb used to express astonishment at something.

clue.text: Seafood (and nothing else) sustains sailor

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting part is below and holds up the sailor

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
alone means and nothing else, solely

explanation.surface: A sailor living on nothing but fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, eaten as a shellfish delicacy.

clue.text: Naughty child learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is learning or traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A naughty child learning how to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead or beseech earnestly.

clue.text: Strangely, T. S. Eliot removes Old Possum's' central character for publication

indicators.note: strangely means the remaining letters come out in an odd order
removes means the letters for old and Possum's centre are taken out of the poet's name before the rearranging
the central character is the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the middle letter of POSSUMS

explanation.surface: Eliot leaves out a main character from Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot wrote Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, which seems to be the book in question. Take O (old) and S, the middle of POSSUMS, out of TSELIOT, and 'Strangely' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishers call each book they issue a title, so a title is a publication.

clue.text: Twirl around, pretty well intoxicated, having consumed whiskey and ecstasy

indicators.note: consumed means taken inside
pretty well means almost all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy spinning round after downing whiskey and taking ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To twiddle is to twist or turn something idly with the fingers.

clue.text: This set of notes describes feature of GATT treaty

definitions.text: This set of notes describes feature of GATT treaty

parts.words: This set of notes describes feature of GATT treaty
parts.note: in music this is a group of three notes; the phrase GATT treaty has three Ts in a row

explanation.walkthrough: GATT is the old General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, but the treaty is a red herring: what counts is the run of three Ts across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a triplet is three notes played in the time of two; generally it is any group of three.

clue.text: Specimen test paper loses everyone at the outset

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: at the outset means take the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: first letter of paper
first letter of loses
first letter of everyone

explanation.surface: A sample exam paper that everyone fails from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test paper' reads as one thing, a mock exam, but 'paper' belongs with the next two words, whose first letters are picked out.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is one item shown as typical of its kind, which is what a specimen is.

clue.text: Celebrate return of personal fortune by Spain

indicators.note: return means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: your lot is your personal fortune in life
X is the sign for 'by', as in multiplication or dimensions
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Spain celebrating a reversal of someone's fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, which is to celebrate someone.

clue.text: Name of lead character? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Name of lead character? Quite the opposite

parts.words: Name of lead character? Quite the opposite
parts.note: swap it round: not the name of the lead character but the lead character of a name, its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: The first half suggests a hero in a novel; 'Quite the opposite' turns it into the first letter of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's initial is the first letter of their name, the leading character.

clue.text: Yahoo accepts sanction over viewpoint

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, holding the other letters inside

parts.note: a yahoo is a boorish lout
to OK something is to sanction it
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A boor agrees to a penalty for an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: A yahoo is a rough, uncouth person, from Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a high place to watch from, a vantage point.

clue.text: Foreign gentleman concealed destination when cycling

parts.note: hid means concealed

indicators.note: cycling means the letters rotate, the first going round to the end

parts.note: a goal is a destination you aim for

explanation.surface: A traveller hides where he is cycling to.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower Spanish nobility, a Spanish gentleman.

clue.text: Communist work wanting first male worker moved because of it?

parts.note: red is a Communist

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and first says the earlier of the two Ms goes

parts.note: employment is work

explanation.surface: A Communist's job in which the first man is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a worker who is moved to a new job has been moved by this.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeployment is moving staff to different jobs or places, so it is why a worker is moved.
